messages.say: Hey there, welcome up to the mountain! I figured grabbing some fresh mountain air and foraging for a few rare greens while we chat beats a stuffy restaurant any day, especially with this golden hour light.
messages.thought: I want to see how he handles stepping away from screens and getting his hands a little dirty right out of the gate.

messages.say: Honestly, you nailed it with this spot—getting outside and breathing in this air is the best way to decompress. I'm all about trading four walls for a bit of real-world adventure, especially when there's good company and golden hour involved. Watch your step over here, these rocks can be a bit tricky, but I think I spot some wild sorrel just past that ridge.
messages.thought: Jenna immediately chose an active, nature-focused setting over a formal dinner, which aligns wonderfully with my appreciation for the outdoors and real-world exploration.

messages.say: You’re right—there’s nothing like a good hike to reset the brain. I love spotting wild sorrel; it reminds me of my own garden—tiny, resilient, and full of color. Speaking of gardens, have you ever tried growing something from seed in the wild?
messages.thought: Gauge his interest in gardening and hands‑on nature activities.

messages.say: I love that—there's something so grounding about watching a garden come together, though my own dirt-under-the-fingernails moments usually happen on Sunday mornings at the griddle rather than the garden bed. I'm all about building things from scratch, whether it's a wild-crafted pancake recipe shaped like a maltipoo for my girls or backing a new venture at Seven Seven Six. Speaking of nurturing things from the ground up, how do you find the mental space to balance running your business and podcast with actually slowing down to enjoy the soil and nature?
messages.thought: I want to see how she balances her high-drive entrepreneurial life with grounding personal routines, making sure she values genuine downtime and family-centric grounding just like I do as a Business Dad.

messages.say: Oh, pancake art for the girls sounds amazing, and honestly, the griddle is just a different kind of canvas! For me, slowing down isn't about finding spare time; it’s a hard boundary I have to draw so I don't lose my mind. I schedule my dirt time just like a board meeting, because if my hands aren't in the soil or I'm not jumping in the lake with my family, I'm just not as good at the work I do. How do you protect your downtime when you’ve got so many massive ventures pulling at your attention?
messages.thought: Testing how he balances his high-intensity entrepreneurial drive with true presence and downtime for family.

messages.say: Scheduling your dirt time like a board meeting is actually brilliant, and honestly, that boundary is so crucial when you're running at our pace. For me, my version of that hard boundary is fiercely protecting my mornings and weekends with my daughters—whether we're inventing wild pancake shapes or heading out to a women's volleyball match. Work will always try to expand to fill every available hour, so you have to be intentional about what you say no to so you can fully show up for the things that actually matter.
messages.thought: She treats her downtime and family connection with the same strategic intentionality that I apply to my 'Business Dad' routines, which is a major green flag.

messages.say: I love that so much—protecting those weekend moments with your girls is the absolute best metric for success, way better than any revenue milestone. I’ve had such a wonderful time hiking with you and trading notes on how we keep ourselves grounded amidst all the building. Let's definitely keep this conversation going over some of those famous pancakes next time!
messages.thought: He really values family time and protects his boundaries, which aligns completely with what I need in a partner.

messages.say: I've genuinely loved this, too, and trading notes on how we protect our grounding while building big things has been refreshing. Consider yourself officially invited to the next Papa Pancake Sunday—just let me know what animal shape you want, and we'll make it happen. Let's definitely keep this going.
messages.thought: She values family boundaries and grounding time just as much as I do, making her a fantastic match for my 'Business Dad' lifestyle and drive.

venue.place: A secluded overlook in the Blue Ridge Mountains during golden hour
venue.activity: Foraging for rare mountain flora, followed by a gourmet campfire pancake dinner cooked on a portable cast iron.
venue.why: It brilliantly bridges Jenna's deep connection to gardening and the land with Alexis's signature weekend tradition of pancake-making for his kids.
